gaps.addiction: No official or 211 list names more than one or two Mesa addiction providers; the only Mesa-specific list of any length is an aggregator (rehabs.org) that mixes nonprofit, AHCCCS and private-pay centres. Match corrections by eye: Mountain Valley Counseling (0.9 to Crossroads), Spero House (0.75 to AZ Fearless Recovery) and National Rehab Hotline (0.67 to a DV hotline) set to none.
gaps.children-pregnancy: No official Mesa list of pregnancy centres; the city's Family Resource Center page names partners without addresses. 211 carried most names, heavy on faith-based pregnancy centres and Phoenix sites; free diapers, formula and baby gear had only one Mesa distributor on any list.
gaps.clothing-household: No official list covers clothing or household goods: the City of Mesa names only Paz de Cristo and Bridging AZ. 211 returns 8 clothing and 8 household-goods results, and the household ones are mostly Phoenix/Peoria. Furniture for the general public is the thinnest: the only Mesa furniture source (Bridging AZ) is agency-referred. findhelp and NeedHelpPayingBills returned 403.
gaps.disability: Disability was the thinnest: City of Mesa pages cover only adaptive recreation and ADA grievances, DES office pages returned 403, and the one regional list is a link sheet from about 2016. Local front doors (DES DDD and VR Mesa offices, Ability360's East Valley office, Mesa ARC-type day programmes) came only from search snippets, not from lists. Match corrections by eye: Maricopa County Disability Services (1.0 to Copa Health), Mesa ADA Coordinator (1.45 to paratransit), Medicare (0.9 to Ability360 Ticket to Work), MCAO Victim Services (0.67 to AG Civil Rights), NFB Arizona (0.67 to iCanConnect) and Southwestern Blind Rehab (0.67 to ACBVI) set to none. Raising Special Kids (0.9 to Encircle Families) was kept but not verified as a rename.
gaps.domestic-violence: DV lists are rich but not Mesa-specific: the City's own two victim-services pages are the fullest and mostly name national hotlines and Phoenix shelters. The biggest finding is staleness: Mesa's homeless-resources page and the CoC sheet still send people to SAFEDVS (1-844-SAFEDVS), which closed 15 May 2026, and the lists give Chrysalis and CPLC the same number. Scout already had nearly everything here; it lacked only love is respect, RedRover, the Family Renewal Center and a separate Mesa Family Advocacy Center entry. Hand corrections: SAFEDVS (tool matched the Deaf Hotline) and Mesa Family Advocacy Center (tool matched the Southwest one) set to none.
gaps.education: Mesa Public Library's adult education pages and the Arizona Department of Education provider list both returned 403, so no official Mesa list was read directly; children's education (tutoring, after-school) had no usable local list at all - the one list found was enrichment programmes in Phoenix.
gaps.employment: No official Mesa list of local employment nonprofits beyond the city's own centre; Mesa Public Library's jobseeker page was blocked (403) and ARIZONA@WORK's resource page too, so 211 carried most names and those skew to Phoenix.
gaps.financial-assistance: Financial assistance lists were mostly utility-bill and rent programmes; no list names a general emergency-cash source in Mesa beyond MesaCAN, the Salvation Army and (by mention) St. Vincent de Paul and Paz de Cristo. 211 results were padded with veteran-only, tribal and other-city programmes, the aggregator carries ended pandemic ERA programmes, and church and congregation help is missing from every list. The Arizona Department of Housing's Maricopa page and findhelp refused to load.
gaps.food: No official City or County food list was readable; all four lists are aggregators. Two of Michael's four yes resources (Fountain of Life Mission Kitchen 153; Chandler-Gilbert CC Coyote Cupboard) are on no list.
gaps.homeless-services: Mesa's official pages name only the City's own line and shelter plus a few phone numbers, and 211's shelter results near Mesa are mostly Phoenix transitional programmes; the only list naming Mesa day services (Streets of Joy, Mesa House, Salvation Army) is a coffee shop's community page. Day centres, meal-and-shower sites and East Valley shelters beyond the Men's Center and I-HELP are where Scout's own search still has to work. Matches corrected by hand: Helaman House (tool picked Autumn House), Tempe HOPE (picked an unrelated outreach), Set Free (none), 211 (re-matched), Safe Place (Scout has two Safe Place entries, Lifeology AZ and Child Crisis Arizona; operator not checked).
gaps.housing: No list names more than a handful of Mesa housing providers: the City's pages cover only its own Housing Authority programmes, and 211's housing results for Mesa are mostly Phoenix senior complexes, veteran-only programmes and legal aid; affordable apartments and non-City rent help in Mesa itself are where Scout's search still has to do the work. Scout's matcher needed eight hand corrections to none here (Emergency Rehab, Fair Housing Center, Housing for Hope, Citadel, Kivel, Retirement Housing Foundation, HUD locator and Pet Housing Help were false matches at 0.6-1.0), and Salvation Army, DES and Veterans First were re-matched to the right agency by hand.
gaps.id-recovery: ID recovery is the thinnest category: no City of Mesa, Maricopa County or state page lists ID help (Mesa's homeless resource list has none), 211 Arizona returned no results for Mesa, and findhelp refused to load. The only lists are the Homeless ID Project's own site list and two small community pages, which between them name four providers; Scout's own search has to do the work here (e.g. MVD, SSA, ADHS fee waivers, shelters' ID help).
gaps.immigration: Only one immigration provider on any list is in Mesa (Immigrant Hope - Mesa); everything else is in Phoenix or Glendale, and the statewide directory pads the count with Tucson, Flagstaff and southern-border offices. No City of Mesa or Maricopa County page lists immigration help; the Mesa library page and the state refugee-programme pages refused to load (403).
gaps.legal: Legal lists were plentiful but repetitive: the official county court lists and 211 name the same countywide Phoenix-based providers (CLS, Arizona Legal Center, AZLawHelp family), and none names a legal-aid office physically in Mesa other than Child Crisis Arizona's clinic; Mesa's own pages are short and point to CLS.
gaps.medical-dental-vision: City of Mesa's own pages name almost no medical, dental or vision providers, and the only state dental list is from 2013; vision was thinnest, with no Mesa provider on any list and 211 returning nothing for eye exams. Match corrections by eye: CARE Partnership (0.67 to Prisma Community Care), New Horizons Dental (0.6 to Donated Dental Services), Healthy Senior Smiles (0.67 to CPLC Healthy Aging), Community Dental Foundation (0.9 to AzDA Give Kids A Smile) and the Mesa prescription card (1.0 to the state AZRx card) were set to none.
gaps.mental-health: City of Mesa lists only four behavioral health names and 211 returned one Mesa provider; the only list naming many East Valley clinics is a 2021 Mercy Care flier. Valleywise Behavioral Health Center Mesa and the East Valley urgent psychiatric centre (CPEC) were on no list read. Match corrections by eye: Crisis Text Line (to Teen Lifeline), Mental Health Guild (0.83 to MHA Arizona), NAZCARE (0.67 to Solari warm line) and Center for Health and Recovery (1.0 to SRPMIC) set to none; Bayless (0.6 to Denova Dobson) was kept because Bayless is now Denova at the same address.
gaps.reentry-support: Reentry lists are the thinnest of the four: no Mesa or East Valley list exists, the County and Sheriff pages give names only, 211 returned nothing in Mesa, the ADCRR reentry page returned 403, and the only Mesa provider any list named (The Mesa House) came from a coffee shop's community page and is missing from Scout. Most names on the lists are Phoenix programmes or general employment and sober-living agencies that fail the main-service rule. Hand corrections: Mesa House, New Horizons, CareerOneStop and Traditions were false matches set to none.
gaps.seniors: No single official Mesa senior resource list; the city names only Aster and a water discount, and the Area Agency on Aging lists only its own programmes. 211's senior results are mostly housing and out-of-area programmes; nothing listed in-home help, transport or caregiver respite from Mesa-based agencies other than Aster.
gaps.transportation: No list names a Mesa-only senior ride programme: the City of Mesa page lists only Valley Metro, and the 'Coupons for Cabs / Mesa Mileage Reimbursement' mentioned in search snippets could not be traced to a live page. 211's list is half AHCCCS member-only rides; the network and aggregator lists are Phoenix and north/west Valley. Valley Metro, findhelp and the DES and azorna pages returned 403.
gaps.utilities-phone-internet: Utility bill help is well listed and consistent (every list sends Mesa residents to MesaCAN and the City's own programmes). Phone and internet are thin: only 211 names any (Lifeline, TruConnect, one Phoenix internet lender); no official Mesa page lists low-cost internet offers such as Cox ConnectAssist, which Scout has only as Cox Lifeline.
gaps.veterans: Lists are plentiful but diluted: the City of Mesa page mixes veteran services with general agencies and national links, and 211 returns mostly VA clinics and national bodies. The main local gap is that no list gives a Mesa walk-in benefits office other than Azura/Mesa VRC and the Vet Center; the ADVS office finder and the Maricopa Community Colleges page returned 403.
